items.title: Taiwan-Based Hacker Used BOSSAI AI Agents to Steal Taipei Emergency Dispatch Records

items.title: Web3Auth Flaw Exploited to Steal Keplr Crypto, Provider Empties Other Wallets for Safety

items.title: isomorphic-git: Path traversal via a ".." tree-entry name writes files outside the working directory on clone/checkout
items.snippet: isomorphic-git's tree parser (`src/models/GitTree.js`) validates each entry name only against the path separators `/` and `\`. It does not reject the standalone reserved name `..`, so a malicious repository can, on a single `clone`/`checkout`, **write files outside the working directory** (unbounded depth). Works on any host-backed `fs` provider. The guard is: ```js // src/models/GitTree.js if (p…
items.summary: isomorphic-git is vulnerable to path traversal via a tree-entry name during clone or checkout, allowing malicious repositories to write files outside the working directory. Upgrade isomorphic-git to 1.38.6 or later.

items.title: isomorphic-git: Circular symbolic references cause non-terminating resolution (DoS)
items.snippet: A malicious server can advertise circular `symref=` capabilities (e.g. `a → b` and `b → a`). isomorphic-git writes them to disk as loose symrefs, and `GitRefManager.resolve()` follows them with no depth limit and no cycle detection, so any later operation that resolves one of them (`log`, `status`, `checkout`, `branch`, …) loops forever — a persistent denial of service from a single clone. `src/m…
items.summary: isomorphic-git is vulnerable to a denial of service via circular symbolic references that cause non-terminating resolution loops. Upgrade isomorphic-git to 1.38.6 or later.

items.title: isomorphic-git: Arbitrary file write outside of working tree via directory symlink during checkout (potential RCE)
items.snippet: `git.checkout` writes working-tree files through a directory symlink without checking the leading path, so a malicious repository can write outside the intended working directory. The defect is in isomorphic-git's checkout logic itself and is therefore independent of the `fs` provider. The *impact* depends on the configured filesystem; worst case is arbitrary file write on the host, e.g. injectin…
items.summary: isomorphic-git allows arbitrary file writes outside the working tree via directory symlinks during checkout, potentially leading to remote code execution. Upgrade isomorphic-git to 1.38.6 or later.

items.title: Moleculer: Unauthenticated Denial of Service via negative length field in the TCP transporter packet parser

A crafted packet whose length field has the sign bit set yields a negative `length`. The parser then advances past the parsed message with `packet = packet.slice(length)`, but `Buffer.prototype.slice` clamps an out-of-range negative start index t…
items.summary: Moleculer contains an unauthenticated denial-of-service vulnerability via a negative length field in the TCP transporter packet parser. Upgrade moleculer to 0.15.2, 0.14.36 or later.

items.title: Locating the source of a mysterious beep with Claude
items.snippet: Our house has a box room, full of boxes that we still haven't unpacked from our last move. A couple of weeks ago something in that room started intermittently beeping. The beeps were far enough apart that standing in the room and trying to determine the source of the noise was frustrating, and I really didn't want to dig through every one of those boxes. So I had Claude Code build Beep Locator, a software system for triangulating the source of a mysterious beep using multiple devices scattered around the room. Here's what Beep Locator looks like after it has been running for a while: You run Python web server to show the primary UI, and then use the QR code or URL to connect as many devices as you can spare to act as listeners - I was using two iPads, a phone, a MacBook Pro and a Surface Ultra. The devices then play noises to each other to help estimate their locations. This didn't work particularly well, so I added a "Rough mode" where you can drag their icons around in the space to provide rough locations which are then adjusted based on those sounds. Once that's set up, the devices all listen for the beep! I added a clapping mode too so I could test it by clapping my hands in d…
items.summary: Simon Willison demonstrates using Claude Code and a Python web server to build a multi-device acoustic triangulation tool for locating a mysterious beep. Try building a utility script with Claude Code to automate a small personal or developer task.
